title: Nikhil Gupta sentenced to over 19 years in prison for plot to kill U.S.-Canadian activist
summary: An Indian man was sentenced to more than 19 years in prison in a federal court in New York on Friday after admitting guilt in a plot to kill dual U.S.-Canadian citizen Gurpatwant Pannun.

image.caption: Nikhil Gupta, accused by U.S. federal prosecutors of plotting with an Indian government official to kill Gurpatwant Singh Pannun, is shown in a June 17, 2024, courtroom sketch in a New York court. (Jane Rosenberg/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New
An Indian man was sentenced to more than 19 years in prison in a federal court in New York on Friday after admitting guilt in a plot to kill dual U.S.-Canadian citizen Gurpatwant Pannun.
Sikh independence activist Gurpatwant Pannun targeted in plot prosecutors say was linked to India intelligence
U.S. District Judge Victor ​Marrero handed down the 235-month sentence for Nikhil Gupta, 55, at a hearing in Manhattan federal ⁠court.

Gupta earlier this year pleaded guilty to murder-for-hire, conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire and conspiracy to commit money laundering in the case. He has been jailed in Brooklyn, N.Y., since his June 2024 extradition to the U.S. from the Czech Republic, where he had been arrested a year earlier.

The plea and sentence on Friday come amid a wave of threats and violence in North America targeting Sikh separatists, headlined by the fatal shooting of Hardeep Singh Nijjar in Surrey, B.C., in June 2023. Then-prime minister Justin Trudeau accused agents of the Indian government of involvement in the killing, which the government in New Delhi denied.
Supporters of an indendent Khalistan are shown outside the federal courthouse building in New York City on Friday, ahead of the sentencing of Gupta. (Kris Reyes/CBC)
Nijjar was a prominent official in Sikhs for Justice, an organization that advocates for a sovereign state in India called Khalistan. Pannun has served as counsel for the group.

"This is the accountability for India's authoritarian [Narendra] Modi regime and this is the first step," said Pannun outside the court before proceedings began. "But we're looking for accountability that all those who directed and financed this assassination plot and my friend's murder in Canada, they should be held responsible."

Prosecutors said an Indian foreign intelligence service ​official, Vikash Yadav, recruited Gupta in May 2023 to orchestrate Pannun's assassination. According to court ⁠papers, Yadav arranged through dealings that Gupta brokered to pay $100,000 US to a purported hitman, who was actually an undercover officer ⁠for the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration, to assassinate Pannun.
Gupta and Yadav arranged to have $15,000 US in cash delivered to the undercover ⁠officer ⁠as an advance payment for the murder, court ​papers show.
"This case cuts to the very core of American ⁠values," prosecutor Ashley Nicolas said in court, according to Reuters. "We don't condone the use of violence to silence ⁠voices ⁠in this country, ever."

items: Prominent Sikh separatist Pannun says RCMP, FBI have contacted him regarding a credible threat

blocks.text: Addressing the ​court, Gupta said he regretted straying from the non-violent example set by Indian independence leader ​Mahatma Gandhi.
"I'm sorry to ⁠Mr. Pannun. I'm sorry to the communities I hurt. I'm sorry to my own family," Gupta said.
Yadav faces an indictment but is not in U.S. custody.
Even with Gupta convicted, Pannun said this summer he had received warnings from the RCMP and FBI about threats to his life under their "duty to warn" protocols.
Pannun sends message to PM Carney

Pannun, who obtained Canadian citizenship in the early 2000s and has maintained a residence in Ontario, told the Associated Press at the time that he was "unfazed and undaunted" by the attempts to silence him.
India's government has denied being involved in the violent incidents.
India Prime Minister Narendra Modi is set to visit Canada on Dec. 11 and 12 and expected to meet with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney.
"Accountability before trade; do not sell the sovereignty of Canada," Pannun said when asked what message he had for Carney.
Suspected Bishnoi gangster wanted in 2023 Winnipeg murder

Four Indian nationals await trial in B.C. in connection with the Nijjar killing after being arrested in Edmonton and Ontario in the spring of 2024. Federal officials in California charged two men earlier this summer with ordering the killing — Lawrence Bishnoi and Satinderjeet Singh, also known as Goldy Brar.
Neither Bihnoi nor Singh are in U.S. custody.
Singh, who is now on FBI's Ten Most Wanted fugitive list, has also just been linked to a 2023 homicide in Winnipeg, which occurred just three months after Nijjar's slaying.
With files from Kris Reyes of CBC News and the Associated Press
